questions.question: When getting ready to change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard, sign, or police officer tells you to do so. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: It is important to slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where pedestrians are present, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take steps to make driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: Signaling your intentions before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other traffic is nearby.
Is a good habit and is required by law.
Is only necessary during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you change lanes or turn. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to tell other drivers your plan.

questions.question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, your vision is limited. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: You are driving when it starts to sleet or snow. You should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead.
Be careful around other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow or sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from the car ahead because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Keep going unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection. Approach at a speed that allows you to slow down if the light changes.

questions.question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your brain and reduces your driving skills. It makes your reactions slower and your judgment worse.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with seat belts give extra protection in front-end crashes. Use both.

questions.question: Is drinking alcohol and driving a serious problem?

options.text: No, it is a minor problem.
Yes, it is a serious problem.
No, it is safe if you have only a few drinks.
No, it is only dangerous to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a serious problem.
questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: What can reduce your ability to drive safely?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and lack of sleep can all reduce your driving ability.

questions.question: You find a defect that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving should be fixed right away. Fix it before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Move to give it a clear path to travel.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to give it a clear path to travel.
questions.explanation: Give emergency vehicles a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: What is important when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal for enough time before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before moving.

questions.question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the red light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: Make turning harder.
Increase hydroplaning risk.
Increase stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning harder and increase stopping distance. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing area. Watch for people crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving in a travel lane:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit.

questions.question: When turning left, you must give the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect driving ability.
Help keep the driver alert.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are distracting activities.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow a flagger's directions in a construction zone. Slow down and use caution as directed. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Yield and let them pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Drive aggressively back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with them makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually makes drivers react more slowly to hazards.
Usually makes drivers drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes drivers react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how quickly a driver reacts to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.
